blocks.alt: Table of every school general fund line, one fiscal year at a time, as two sums: the school budget to what was left, with cost moved to other funds by journal entry apart from what it spent; and what the line cost from every fund. Sortable by category and by every column

basis.label: Our placing of other funds’ spending on the lines

columns.label: Voted
columns.means: What Town Meeting voted for this line in the school budget.

columns.label: Transfers in or out
columns.means: Budget moved between lines during the year: permission to spend moves from one line to another. No bill moves.

columns.label: Carried from last year
columns.means: Last year’s unpaid orders, carried in with the budget to pay them.

columns.label: Budget
columns.means: What the line was allowed to spend: voted, plus transfers, plus carried.

columns.label: Spent before re-charges
columns.means: What the school budget paid or still owed on this line, before any bill was re-charged to or from another fund. Orders still owed at year end count.

columns.label: Re-charged to other funds
columns.means: The school budget paid these bills first. Later another fund paid it back the same amount. So the school budget spent less, and Left goes up.

columns.label: Re-charged from other funds
columns.means: Another fund paid these bills first. Later the school budget paid it back. So the school budget spent more, and Left goes down.

columns.label: Left
columns.means: The budget, less what the school budget spent after the re-charges: this line’s part of the surplus, or of what ran over.

columns.label: Spent by the school budget
columns.means: What the school budget spent on this line, after the re-charges.

columns.label: Paid by other funds, re-charged later
columns.means: The same bills as Re-charged to other funds: the school budget paid first, and another fund paid it back. They still count here, because they are still part of what this line cost.

columns.label: Paid by other funds, from the start
columns.means: Another fund paid these bills itself; the school budget never did, so Left does not change. Which bills count toward this line is our match, by payee or by kind of work.

columns.label: Total spent, all funds
columns.means: What the line cost, from every fund.

groups.label: What the line cost, every fund

text.between: the lines in between: show every line
text.chip_direct: Paid by other funds, from the start
text.cost_sum: What the line cost, every fund
text.footing: Spent counts orders still owed at year end, so for FY2025 and earlier Left can differ from the Town’s printed report by those orders.
text.none: No other fund paid toward this line.
text.other_funds: Other funds: grants, the circuit breaker, fees and revolving funds, and capital articles. Re-charges are the Town’s own entries; which spending counts as paid from the start toward a line is our match, by payee or by kind of work.
text.payers: Other funds that paid toward this line
text.read: Other funds can pay a line’s bills in two ways, and only one of them changes Left. The school budget can pay first and a journal entry RE-CHARGE the bills to a grant or another fund later: the school budget’s spending falls and Left rises, and the line cost the same. Or the other fund can pay FROM THE START: Left is untouched, and the line cost more than the school budget shows. Hover or tap a circled amount to see each entry.
text.shared: Many lines gave and many got in this one entry, and the books do not say which line’s money went to which. The other side, all together:
text.unmatched: Other funds’ spending not matched to any line

so.text: A line can end under because its bills were re-charged to another fund after the school budget paid them. Sorted by category, lines that cancel each other out sit side by side.

blocks.title: Every line, budget and cost

blocks.alt: Alluvial diagram, four fiscal years: what the school budget’s lines cost from every fund, in seven blocks, each split by who paid, with bands joining each block and payer from year to year

basis.label: Our placing of other funds’ spending on the lines

groups.label: Other funds, not matched to a line

data.note: What each block cost from every fund, by who paid. School general fund lines, department 300, with other funds’ spending placed on them by the match rules below; grey is what no rule places. Orders still owed are counted.

so.text: Follow a band: one that keeps its height and changes colour is a cost that held while its payer changed, the move a voted budget cannot show.

blocks.title: Who paid for what, year by year

blocks.alt: Flow diagram, one year at a time: every category whose lines ended under budget flows into one pool on the left; the pool flows out to every category whose lines ran over, and what remains is what was left

basis.label: What each line had left, as the journal records it

text.read: Nothing in the books says which leftover paid for which overrun: inside one appropriation the money is a pool. So no line is drawn from one to another.
text.transfers: Moved between lines by transfer, both ends named (on the timeline):

so.text: The overruns were paid from leftovers in general, not from any one of them. A claim that one line covered another is a reading, not a record.

blocks.title: One pool, not pairs

so.text: When a move was made shows whether it was planned or a year-end adjustment. In FY2026 most of the money moved in the last five weeks.

blocks.title: Every recorded move, dated

paragraphs.text: **Voted above cost** is the vote, less what the line cost from every fund. **Paid by other funds** is what grants, the circuit breaker, fees and revolving funds paid toward the line. **Transfers** moved budget between lines. **Another year’s money** is orders carried in from last year, less what they paid, less next year’s bills paid early.

Which other-fund dollar counts toward which line is our reading, in order: a journal entry naming both ends, then the same payee, then the same function code (placed on a category, never a line). What none of them places is shown apart, never counted as voted above cost. Capital articles are matched only by a journal entry.

blocks.title: How the four parts are counted

note.text: The first two steps are our placing of other funds’ spending; their sum is measured. The last two are postings. School general fund, department 300.

chart.title: From the vote to what was left

so.text: A line is what is left after other funds pay, so it can end under with nothing costing less. They paid $102,204 more than in FY2025.

conclusions.text: Other funds paid $1,538,180 toward FY2026’s lines; the vote alone was $921,081 below what they cost.

so.text: One grant changed payer both ways in one year; the voted budget shows neither. Why it paid the placement is in no document held.

conclusions.text: The IDEA grant paid $287,108 of private tuition; June entries moved $205,645 of its pay onto the general fund.

so.text: A swing of $620,281 between two years, made by entries after the spending. Each is in the journal with its date and memo.

conclusions.text: Journal entries took a net $366,899 off the general fund in FY2026, after adding $253,382 in FY2025.

so.text: Without the early payment FY2026 would have left $671,395, more than FY2025 on the same footing.

conclusions.text: FY2026 paid $189,277 of FY2027 tuition; $41,377 of FY2025’s orders were carried in and never paid.
